# Sirach Chapter 40 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 40 | **Agents Consulted:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 40 opens with one of Ben Sira's bleakest passages — a meditation on universal human misery that recalls Ecclesiastes. The long opening period (vv. 1–7) sweeps from king to pauper, noting that sleep itself brings no relief. Verse 8 limits the darkest things to sinners sevenfold. The chapter then pivots to the "better than" wisdom sayings (vv. 18–27), a structured series of escalating comparisons in which the fear of the Lord tops every list (v. 26). The chapter closes with a sharp warning about begging: "it is better to die than to beg" (v. 28) — one of Ben Sira's most quoted lines, reflecting ancient Mediterranean honor culture. The closing image (v. 30) of begging as sweet in the mouth but fire in the stomach echoes Proverbs 9's wisdom vs. folly contrast.

---

40:1 Much hardship has been created for every human being, and a heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam from the day they come forth from their mother's womb until the day they return to the mother of all the living.

40:2 Perplexity and fear of heart, anxious imagination and the day of death —

40:3 from the one who sits on a glorious throne to the one laid low in dust and ashes,

40:4 from the one arrayed in purple and a crown to the one clothed in coarse linen —

40:5 wrath and envy and trouble and restlessness and fear of death and rage and strife. And when one lies on his bed to rest, his sleep at night confuses his mind.

40:6 He gets little or no rest; as in a night watch he is disturbed in his sleep: sometimes by the terror of a nightmare, sometimes sinking into a stupor with but a brief moment of relief — as if rescued from the day of battle.

40:7 He rouses himself and marvels that the terror was nothing at all.

40:8 Such things happen to all creatures, human beings and animals, but for sinners sevenfold.

40:9 Death and bloodshed and strife and sword, calamities, famine and ruin and plague —

40:10 all these were created for the wicked, and it is because of them that the Flood came.

40:11 All things that are from the earth return to the earth, and what comes from the waters returns to the sea.

40:12 All bribery and injustice will be wiped out, but faithfulness will stand forever.

40:13 The wealth of the unjust dries up like a wadi and vanishes like a mighty thunderclap.

40:14 A generous man will rejoice, but transgressors will utterly fail.

40:15 The children of the ungodly will not put out many branches, and impure roots stand on crumbling rock.

40:16 The reeds along every riverbank will be uprooted before all other grass.

40:17 Kindness is like a garden of blessing, and almsgiving endures forever.

40:18 The life of a laborer who is self-sufficient is sweet, but better than both is the one who finds a treasure.

40:19 Children and the founding of a city preserve a name, but better than both is the one who finds wisdom. Cattle and orchards make a man prosperous, but better than both is a beloved wife.

40:20 Wine and music gladden the heart, but better than both is the love of wisdom.

40:21 The flute and the harp make melody, but better than both is a pleasant voice.

40:22 The eye desires grace and beauty, but better than both are the green shoots of grain.

40:23 A friend and a companion are welcome at the right time, but better than both is a wife with her husband.

40:24 Brothers and helpers are for a time of trouble, but charitable giving rescues better than both.

40:25 Gold and silver make one's footing secure, but better than both is good counsel.

40:26 Riches and strength lift up the heart, but better than both is the fear of the Lord. In the fear of the Lord there is no want, and there is no need to seek any other support.

40:27 The fear of the Lord is a garden of blessing, and it covers a person with more glory than any canopy.

40:28 My child, do not lead the life of a beggar; it is better to die than to beg.

40:29 When one looks to another's table for sustenance, that existence cannot truly be called a life. One defiles oneself with another's food, but the intelligent and well-instructed person guards against this.

40:30 In the mouth of the shameless, begging is sweet, but in his stomach a fire is kindled.
